claim: Insect navigation arises from the coordinated action of concurrent guidance systems.
source: Insect navigation arises from the coordinated action of concurrent guidance systems but the neural mechanisms through which each functions, and are then coordinated, remains unknown.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a foundational premise of the work.

claim: The neural mechanisms through which insect guidance systems function and are coordinated remain unknown.
source: Insect navigation arises from the coordinated action of concurrent guidance systems but the neural mechanisms through which each functions, and are then coordinated, remains unknown.
evidence: This is stated as a knowledge gap in the abstract.

claim: Insects require distinct strategies to retrace familiar routes (route-following) and directly return from novel to familiar terrain (homing).
source: We propose that insects require distinct strategies to retrace familiar routes (route-following) and directly return from novel to familiar terrain (homing) using different aspects of frequency encoded views that are processed in different neural pathways.
evidence: This is a core proposal of the model presented in the abstract.

claim: Route-following and homing use different aspects of frequency encoded views that are processed in different neural pathways.
source: We propose that insects require distinct strategies to retrace familiar routes (route-following) and directly return from novel to familiar terrain (homing) using different aspects of frequency encoded views that are processed in different neural pathways.
evidence: This is a core proposal of the model presented in the abstract.

claim: The Central Complex and Mushroom Bodies regions of the insect brain may work in tandem to coordinate the directional output of different guidance cues.
source: We also demonstrate how the Central Complex and Mushroom Bodies regions of the insect brain may work in tandem to coordinate the directional output of different guidance cues through a contextually switched ring-attractor inspired by neural recordings.
evidence: This is stated as a demonstration in the abstract.

claim: The coordination of guidance cues occurs through a contextually switched ring-attractor inspired by neural recordings.
source: We also demonstrate how the Central Complex and Mushroom Bodies regions of the insect brain may work in tandem to coordinate the directional output of different guidance cues through a contextually switched ring-attractor inspired by neural recordings.
evidence: This is stated as a demonstration in the abstract, drawing on neural recordings.

claim: The unified model of insect navigation reproduces behavioural data from a series of cue conflict experiments in realistic animal environments.
source: The resultant unified model of insect navigation reproduces behavioural data from a series of cue conflict experiments in realistic animal environments and offers testable hypotheses of where and how insects process visual cues, utilise the different information that they provide and coordinate their outputs to achieve the adaptive behaviours observed in the wild.
evidence: This is stated as a result in the abstract.

claim: Central-place foraging insects navigate using a 'toolkit' of independent guidance systems.
source: Central-place foraging insects navigate using a 'toolkit' of independent guidance systems (Wehner, 2009)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation to Wehner, 2009.

claim: Path integration is a fundamental guidance system whereby foragers track the distance and direction to their nest by integrating the series of directions and distances travelled.
source: of which the most fundamental are path integration (PI), whereby foragers track the distance and direction to their nest by integrating the series of directions and distances travelled (for reviews see Heinze et al., 2018; Collett, 2019)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to review papers.

claim: Visual memory is a fundamental guidance system whereby foragers derive a homing signal by comparing the difference between current and stored views.
source: and visual memory (VM), whereby foragers derive a homing signal by comparing the difference between current and stored views (for reviews see Zeil, 2012; Collett et al., 2013)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to review papers.

claim: The central complex neuropil (CX) is advocated as the path integration centre.
source: Neurophysiological and computational modelling studies advocate the central complex neuropil (CX) as the PI centre (Heinze and Homberg, 2007; Seelig and Jayaraman, 2015; Stone et al., 2017)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to neurophysiological and computational studies.

claim: The mushroom body neuropils (MB) appear well suited to assessing visual valence as needed for visual memory.
source: whereas the mushroom body neuropils (MB) appear well suited to assessing visual valence as needed for VM (Heisenberg, 2003; Ardin et al., 2016; Müller et al., 2018)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to relevant studies.

claim: Current visual memory models based on the MB architecture can replicate route following behaviours.
source: although current VM models based on the MB architecture can replicate route following (RF) behaviours whereby insects visually recognise the direction previously travelled at the same position (Ardin et al., 2016; Müller et al., 2018)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to specific models.

claim: Current visual memory models based on the MB architecture cannot account for visual homing behaviours whereby insects return directly to their familiar surroundings from novel locations.
source: they cannot account for visual homing (VH) behaviours whereby insects return directly to their familiar surroundings from novel locations following a displacement (e.g. after being blown off course by a gust of wind) (Wystrach et al., 2012)
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of current models in the introduction with citation.

claim: Premotor regions of the CX coordinate navigation behaviour.
source: despite increasing neuroanatomical evidence suggesting that premotor regions of the CX coordinate navigation behaviour (Pfeiffer and Homberg, 2014; Heinze and Pfeiffer, 2018; Honkanen et al., 2019)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to neuroanatomical studies.

claim: A theoretical hypothesis explaining how the CX coordinates navigation behaviour through neural circuitry has yet to be developed.
source: a theoretical hypothesis explaining how this is achieved by the neural circuitry has yet to be developed
evidence: This is stated as a knowledge gap in the introduction.

claim: The unified neural navigation model extends the core guidance modules from two (PI and VM) to three (PI, RF, and VH).
source: In this work, we present a unified neural navigation model that extends the core guidance modules from two (PI and VM) to three (PI, RF, and VH)
evidence: This is stated as a contribution of the work in the introduction.

claim: The unified model integrates the outputs of PI, RF, and VH optimally using a biologically realistic ring attractor network in the CX to produce realistic homing behaviours.
source: and by integrating their outputs optimally using a biologically realistic ring attractor network in the CX produces realistic homing behaviours
evidence: This is stated as a contribution of the work in the introduction.

claim: Contemporary VM models based on the MBs can replicate realistic RF behaviours in complex visual environments.
source: Contemporary VM models based on the MBs can replicate realistic RF behaviours in complex visual environments (ant environments: Kodzhabashev and Mangan, 2015; Ardin et al., 2016, bee environments: Müller et al., 2018)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to specific studies.

claim: Contemporary VM models do not generalise to visual homing scenarios whereby the animal must return directly to familiar terrain from novel locations.
source: but do not generalise to visual homing scenarios whereby the animal must return directly to familiar terrain from novel locations (ants: Narendra, 2007, bees: Cartwright and Collett, 1982, wasps: Stürzl et al., 2016)
evidence: This is stated as a limitation in the introduction with citations to behavioral studies.

claim: Insects store multiple nest-facing views before foraging, inspired by observed learning walks in ants and flights in bees and wasps.
source: Storing multiple nest-facing views before foraging, inspired by observed learning walks in ants (Müller and Wehner, 2010; Fleischmann et al., 2016) and flights in bees and wasps (Zeil et al., 1996; Zeil and Fleischmann, 2019), provides a potential solution (Graham et al., 2010; Wystrach et al., 2013)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to behavioral and modeling studies.

claim: Storing multiple nest-facing views is brittle due to high probabilities of aligning with the wrong memory causing catastrophic errors.
source: but simulation studies have found this approach to be brittle due to high probabilities of aligning with the wrong memory causing catastrophic errors (Dewar et al., 2014)
evidence: This is stated as a limitation in the introduction with citation to a simulation study.

claim: Ants released perpendicularly to their familiar route do not generally align with their familiar visual direction as predicted by current algorithms.
source: Moreover, ants released perpendicularly to their familiar route do not generally align with their familiar visual direction as predicted by the above algorithms (Wystrach et al., 2012)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation to a behavioral study.

claim: Ants released perpendicularly to their familiar route move directly back towards the route.
source: but instead move directly back towards the route (Fukushi and Wehner, 2004; Kohler and Wehner, 2005; Narendra, 2007; Mangan and Webb, 2012; Wystrach et al., 2012)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to multiple behavioral studies.

claim: Desert ants integrate their PI and VH outputs in a manner consistent with optimal integration theory by weighting VH relative to the familiarity of the current view.
source: In such scenarios, desert ants strike a comprise by integrating their PI and VH outputs in a manner consistent with optimal integration theory by weighting VH relative to the familiarity of the current view (Legge et al., 2014)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation to a behavioral study.

claim: Desert ants weight PI relative to the home vector length (a proxy for directional certainty).
source: and PI relative to the home vector length (a proxy for directional certainty) (Wystrach et al., 2015)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation to a behavioral study.

claim: Ring-like structures of the CX represent directional cues as bumps of activity with the peak defining the specific target direction.
source: Various ring-like structures of the CX represent directional cues as bumps of activity with the peak defining the specific target direction, and the spread providing a mechanism to encode cue certainty as required for optimal integration
evidence: This is stated in the introduction drawing on knowledge of CX structure.

claim: The spread of activity in CX ring-like structures provides a mechanism to encode cue certainty as required for optimal integration.
source: Various ring-like structures of the CX represent directional cues as bumps of activity with the peak defining the specific target direction, and the spread providing a mechanism to encode cue certainty as required for optimal integration (for an example see increased spread of HD cell activity when only proprioceptive cues are present [Seelig and Jayaraman, 2015])
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation to a neurophysiological study.

claim: Ring attractors provide a biologically realistic means to optimally weight cues represented in bump-of-activity format.
source: Besides their excellent properties to encode the animal's heading ring attractors also provide a biologically realistic means to optimally weight cues represented in this format (Touretzky, 2005; Mangan and Yue, 2018) without the need for dedicated memory circuits to store means and uncertainties of each cue.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to theoretical studies.

claim: A pair of integrating ring-attractor networks in the CX are sufficient for optimally weighting multiple directional cues from the same frame of reference.
source: Thus we introduce a pair of integrating ring-attractor networks to the CX model (Figure 3A grey neural rings: RA_L and RA_R) that take as input the desired headings from the above proposed VH model (red neural rings: VH_L and VH_R) and Stone et al., 2017's PI model (orange neural rings: PI_L and PI_R) and output combined Off Route desired heading signals that are sent to the steering circuits (blue neural rings: CPU_L and CPU_R).
evidence: This is stated as a model contribution in the introduction.

claim: Stone et al., 2017 mapped the home vector computation to a population of neurons (CPU4) owing to their dual inputs from direction selective compass neurons (I_TB1) and motion-sensitive speed neurons (TN2) as well as their recurrent connectivity patterns facilitating accumulation of activity.
source: Stone et al., 2017 mapped the home vector computation to a population of neurons (CPU4) owing to their dual inputs from direction selective compass neurons (I_TB1) and motion-sensitive speed neurons (TN2) as well as their recurrent connectivity patterns facilitating accumulation of activity as the animal moves in a given direction.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation to Stone et al., 2017.

claim: The certainty of PI automatically scales with the home-vector length owing to the accumulating effect of the memory neurons which correlates with directional uncertainty.
source: Wystrach et al., 2015 showed that the certainty of PI automatically scales with the home-vector length owing to the accumulating effect of the memory neurons which correlates with directional uncertainty
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation to Wystrach et al., 2015.

claim: The model replicates the trends reported in cue-conflict experiments by Legge et al., 2014 and Wystrach et al., 2015 when the uncertainty of PI and VH cues were altered independently.
source: Figure 3C shows the initial headings produced by the model which replicates the trends reported in cue-conflict experiments by Legge et al., 2014 and Wystrach et al., 2015 when the uncertainty of PI and VH cues were altered independently.
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 3C showing model output matching behavioral data.

claim: Binary images of panoramic skylines converted into their frequency components can provide rotationally-invariant encoding of scenes in a compact form.
source: Stone et al., 2018 recently demonstrated that binary images of panoramic skylines converted into their frequency components can provide such a rotationally-invariant encoding of scenes in a compact form (see Image processing for an introduction to frequency transformations of images).
evidence: This is stated in the results with citation to Stone et al., 2018.

claim: The difference between the rotationally invariant features (the amplitudes of the frequency coefficients) between two locations increases monotonically with distance producing an error surface suitable for visual homing.
source: Moreover, they demonstrated that the difference between the rotationally invariant features (the amplitudes of the frequency coefficients) between two locations increases monotonically with distance producing an error surface reminiscent of the image difference surfaces reported by Zeil et al., 2003 which can guide an agent back to familiar terrain.
evidence: This is stated in the results with citations to Stone et al., 2018 and Zeil et al., 2003.

claim: The MB neuropils can assess the visual valence of learned rotationally-varying panoramic skylines for route following.
source: Here we investigate whether the MB neuropils shown capable of assessing the visual valence of learned rotationally-varying panoramic skylines for RF (Ardin et al., 2016; Müller et al., 2018), might instead assess the visual valence of rotationally-invariant properties of views sampled along a familiar route supporting visual homing.
evidence: This is stated in the results with citations to previous models.

claim: The firing rate of the MB output neuron (MBON) when placed at locations across the environment at random orientations reveals a gradient that increases monotonically with distance from the familiar route area.
source: After training, the firing rate of the MB output neuron (MBON) when placed at locations across the environment at random orientations reveals a gradient that increases monotonically with distance from the familiar route area, providing a homing signal sufficient for VH independent of the animal's orientation (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 2C showing the gradient.

claim: The proposed VH network accurately replicates both the directed initial paths and extended homing paths observed in ants displaced to novel locations perpendicular to their familiar routes.
source: Figure 2D demonstrates that the proposed network accurately replicates both the directed initial paths as in Wystrach et al., 2012 (see the inserted black arrow), and extended homing paths as in Narendra, 2007 observed in ants displaced to novel locations perpendicular to their familiar routes.
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 2D and citations to behavioral studies.

claim: Upon encountering the route the VH model is unable to distinguish the direction in which to travel and thus meanders back and forth along the familiarity valley.
source: We note that upon encountering the route the model is unable to distinguish the direction in which to travel and thus meanders back and forth along the familiarity valley, unlike real ants, demonstrating the need for additional route recognition and recovery capabilities.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of the VH model in the results.

claim: The RF model accurately recovers the initial route heading in a similar manner to real ants returned to the start of their familiar route.
source: The RF model accurately recovers the initial route heading in a similar manner to real ants returned to the start of their familiar route (Wystrach et al., 2012; Figure 4B, insert)
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 4B and citation to behavioral study.

claim: The RF model follows the remaining route in its entirety back to the nest reflecting ant data.
source: and then follows the remaining route in its entirety back to the nest again reflecting ant data (Kohler and Wehner, 2005; Mangan and Webb, 2012; Figure 4B)
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 4B and citations to behavioral studies.

claim: The unified model accurately replicates the initial headings produced in cue-conflict experiments when the uncertainty of PI and VH cues were altered independently.
source: Figure 3C shows the initial headings produced by the model which replicates the trends reported in cue-conflict experiments by Legge et al., 2014 and Wystrach et al., 2015 when the uncertainty of PI and VH cues were altered independently.
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 3C and citations to behavioral studies.

claim: The combined PI and VH model shows the most ant-like behaviour by initially following predominantly the home-vector direction before switching to visual homing when the home-vector length drops.
source: Example extended paths of independent PI and VH models and the ring-attractor-based combined PI and VH model are plotted in Figure 3D with the combined model showing the most ant-like behaviour (Kohler and Wehner, 2005; Mangan and Webb, 2012) by initially following predominantly the home-vector direction before switching to visual homing when the home-vector length drops leading the simulated ant back to familiar terrain.
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 3D and citations to behavioral studies.

claim: The activity of the proposed switching circuit and the paths that it generates in simulated zero vector and full vector displacement trials replicate context-dependent behavioral switching.
source: The activity of the proposed switching circuit and the paths that it generates in simulated zero vector and full vector displacement trials are shown in Figure 5B and C respectively.
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 5B and C showing model behavior.

claim: The proposed unified navigation model can fulfil all of the criteria defined for replication of key adaptive behaviour observed in insects.
source: It should be noted that the data presented utilised different activation functions of the TUN neuron that weights PI and VH (see Table 1 for parameter settings across trials and Discussion for insights into model limitations and potential extensions), yet the results presented nevertheless provide a proof-of-principle demonstration that the proposed unified navigation model can fulfil all of the criteria defined for replication of key adaptive behaviour observed in insects (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the results section.

claim: The insect navigation toolkit should be extended to include independent visual homing (VH) and route following (RF) systems.
source: We propose that the insect navigation toolkit (Wehner, 2009; Webb, 2019) should be extended to include independent visual homing (VH) and route following (RF) systems (see Figure 1B for updated Insect Navigation Toolkit).
evidence: This is stated as a proposal in the discussion.

claim: VH and RF can be realised using frequency-encoding of panoramic skylines to separate information into rotationally invariant amplitudes for VH and rotationally varying phases for RF.
source: We show how VH and RF can be realised using frequency-encoding of panoramic skylines to separate information into rotationally invariant amplitudes for VH and rotationally varying phases for RF.
evidence: This is stated as a demonstration in the discussion.

claim: Behavioural studies support the use of spatial frequency by bees.
source: The current model utilises frequency encoding schema from the computer graphics but behavioural studies support the use of spatial frequency by bees (Horridge, 1997; Lehrer, 1999)
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citations to behavioral studies.

claim: Neurons in the lobula of dragonflies and locusts have receptive fields akin to basis functions, providing a mechanism to extract frequency information.
source: with neurons in the lobula of dragonflies (O'Carroll, 1993) and locusts James and Osorio, 1996 found to have receptive fields akin to basis functions, providing a mechanism by which to extract the frequency information necessary for the local compass system.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citations to neurophysiological studies.

claim: Visual homing is modelled on neural circuits found along the OL-MB-SMP pathway before terminating in the CX steering circuit.
source: Visual homing is modelled on neural circuits found along the OL-MB-SMP pathway (Ehmer and Gronenberg, 2002; Gronenberg and López-Riquelme, 2004) before terminating in the CX steering circuit (Stone et al., 2017) and shown capable of producing realistic homing paths.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citations to neuroanatomical and modeling studies.

claim: The MBs output 'whether' the current sensory stimulus is positive or negative and the CX then adapts the animal heading accordingly.
source: This is inline with the hypothesis forwarded by Collett and Collett, 2018 that suggest that the MBs output 'whether' the current sensory stimulus is positive or negative and the CX then adapts the animal heading, the 'whither', accordingly.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citation to Collett and Collett, 2018.

claim: Route following is shown possible by learned associations between the amplitudes (i.e. the place) and the phase (the orientation) experienced along a route.
source: Route following is shown possible by learned associations between the amplitudes (i.e. the place) and the phase (the orientation) experienced along a route, allowing realignment when later at a proximal location.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a demonstration.

claim: Neural plasticity-based correlation between the visual surroundings and the orientations fits with data recently observed in fruit flies.
source: This kind of neural plasticity-based correlation between the visual surroundings and the orientations fits with data recently observed in fruit flies (Kim et al., 2019; Fisher et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citations to recent studies.

claim: The layered visual pathway from OL via AOTU and BU to the EB of the CX with its suggested neural plasticity properties provides a possible neural pathway for route following.
source: Neurophysiological evidence suggests that the layered visual pathway from OL via AOTU and BU to the EB of the CX (Barth and Heisenberg, 1997; Homberg et al., 2003; Omoto et al., 2017) with its suggested neural plasticity properties (Barth and Heisenberg, 1997; Yilmaz et al., 2019) provides a possible neural pathway
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citations to neurophysiological studies.

claim: The model hypothesises that insects possess different compass systems based on varied sensory information.
source: Our model therefore hypothesises that insects possess different compass systems based on varied sensory information and further that insects possess the capability (via CX-based RAs) to coordinate their influence optimally according to the current context.
evidence: This is stated as a hypothesis in the discussion.

claim: Insects possess the capability (via CX-based RAs) to coordinate the influence of different compass systems optimally according to the current context.
source: Our model therefore hypothesises that insects possess different compass systems based on varied sensory information and further that insects possess the capability (via CX-based RAs) to coordinate their influence optimally according to the current context.
evidence: This is stated as a hypothesis in the discussion.

claim: A pair of ring attractor networks that have similar connectivity patterns of the CX-based head-direction system are sufficient for optimally weighting multiple directional cues from the same frame of reference.
source: Specifically, we demonstrate that a pair of ring attractor networks that have similar connectivity patterns of the CX-based head-direction system (Kim et al., 2017; Turner-Evans et al., 2019; Pisokas et al., 2019), are sufficient for optimally weighting multiple directional cues from the same frame of reference (e.g. VH and PI).
evidence: This is stated as a demonstration in the discussion with citations to neurophysiological studies.

claim: The use of a pair of integrating RAs is inspired by the column structure of the FB which has 16 neural columns divided into two groups of 8 neural columns that each represent the entire 360° space.
source: The use of a pair of integrating RAs is inspired by the column structure of the FB which has 16 neural columns divided into two groups of 8 neural columns that each represent the entire 360°space.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an inspiration for the model architecture.

claim: The optimal integration of PI and VH using a ring attractor closely matches the networks theorised to govern optimal directional integration in mammals.
source: The optimal integration of PI and VH using a ring attractor closely matches the networks theorised to govern optimal directional integration in mammals (Jeffery et al., 2016) and supports hypothesis of their conserved use across animals (Mangan and Yue, 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citations to theoretical studies.

claim: The network includes three independent ring attractor networks: the global compass head direction system, the local compass head direction system, and an Off-route integration system.
source: To replicate the suite of navigational behaviours described in Figure 1, our network includes three independent ring attractor networks: the global compass head direction system Pisokas et al., 2019; the local compass head direction system (Seelig and Jayaraman, 2015; Kim et al., 2017; Turner-Evans et al., 2019); and an Off-route integration system (modelled here).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citations to neurophysiological studies.

claim: Central place foraging insects likely possess a similar integration network for 'On-Route' cues bringing the total number of RAs to four.
source: We would speculate that it is likely that central place foraging insects also possess a similar integration network for 'On-Route' cues (not modelled here) bringing the total number of RAs to four.
evidence: This is stated as speculation in the discussion.

claim: The adaptive behaviour demonstrated is the result of distinct guidance systems that converge in the CX, with their relative weighting defined by the output of the MB.
source: In summary, the adaptive behaviour demonstrated is the result of distinct guidance systems that converge in the CX, with their relative weighting defined by the output of the MB.
evidence: This is stated as a summary in the discussion.

claim: The distributed architecture is reminiscent of mechanisms found in the visual learning of honeybees.
source: This distributed architecture is reminiscent of mechanisms found in the visual learning of honeybees (Plath et al., 2017)
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citation to a study on honeybees.

claim: The CX is the navigation coordinator of insects.
source: and supports the hypothesis that the CX is the navigation coordinator of insects (Heinze, 2017; Honkanen et al., 2019)
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citations to review papers.

claim: The MB acts as a mediator allowing the CX to generate optimal behaviour according to the context.
source: but shows how the MB acts as a mediator allowing the CX to generate optimal behaviour according to the context.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an insight from the model.

claim: The resultant unified model of insect navigation represents a proof-of-principle framework as to how insects might co-ordinate core navigational behaviours (PI, VH and RF) under standard field manipulations.
source: The resultant unified model of insect navigation Figure 1B and C represents a proof-of-principle framework as to how insects might co-ordinate core navigational behaviours (PI, VH and RF) under standard field manipulations Figure 1A.
evidence: This is stated as a summary in the discussion.

claim: The framework can be easily extended to new navigation behaviours observed in other insects from idiothetic PI to straight line following to migrations.
source: The framework can be easily extended to new navigation behaviours observed in other insects from idiothetic PI (Kim and Dickinson, 2017) to straight line following El Jundi et al., 2016 to migrations (Reppert et al., 2016) as well as more nuanced strategies that flexibly use directional cues from different sensory modalities (Wystrach et al., 2013; Schwarz et al., 2017; Dacke et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citations to various studies.

claim: The environment used in this study is adapted from Baddeley et al., 2012.
source: The environment used in this study is that provided by Stone et al., 2018 which is itself adapted from Baddeley et al., 2012 (see Figure 7C).
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section with citations.

claim: The simulated world is a virtual ant-like world consisting of randomly generated bushes, trees and tussocks based on triangular patches.
source: It is a virtual ant-like world consisting of randomly generated bushes, trees and tussocks based on triangular patches (for more details see Baddeley et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section with citation.

claim: Image compression algorithms such as JPEG encoding have long utilised the fact that a complex signal can be decomposed into a series of trigonometric functions that oscillate at different frequencies.
source: Image compression algorithms such as JPEG encoding Hudson et al., 2018 have long utilised the fact that a complex signal can be decomposed into a series of trigonometric functions that oscillate at different frequencies.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section with citation.

claim: For panoramic views, regardless of the rotational angle of the image capturing device the entire signal will always be visible and hence the amplitudes of the frequency coefficients do not alter with rotation.
source: For panoramic views, regardless of the rotational angle of the image capturing device (eye or camera) the entire signal will always be visible and hence the amplitudes of the frequency coefficients do not alter with rotation (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section with reference to Figure 7B.

claim: The amplitudes of frequency coefficients have been used for successful place recognition in a series of robot studies.
source: This information has been used for successful place recognition in a series of robot studies (Pajdla and Hlaváč, 1999; Menegatti et al., 2004; Stone et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section with citations to robot studies.

claim: The phase of each coefficient describes how to align the signal and will naturally track any rotation in the panoramic view providing a means to realign with previous headings.
source: In addition, as the phase of each coefficient describes how to align the signal this will naturally track any rotation in the panoramic view (Figure 7B) providing a means to realign with previous headings.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section with reference to Figure 7B.

claim: The phase components of panoramic images have been utilised previously to derive the home direction in a visual homing task.
source: The phase components of panoramic images have been utilised previously to derive the home direction in a visual homing task (Stürzl and Mallot, 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section with citation.

claim: Zernike Moments are defined as the projection of a function onto orthogonal basis polynomials called Zernike polynomials.
source: Zernike Moments (ZM) are defined as the projection of a function onto orthogonal basis polynomials called Zernike polynomials (Teague, 1980; Khotanzad and Hong, 1990).
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section with citations.

claim: The global compass neural network applied in this study is the same as that of Stone et al., 2017.
source: The global compass neural network applied in this study is the same as that of Stone et al., 2017, which has three layers of neurons: TL neurons, CL1 neurons and I-TB1 neurons.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section with citation.

claim: The 8 I-TB1 neurons act as a ring attractor creating a sinusoidal encoding of the current heading.
source: The 8 I-TB1 neurons act as a ring attractor creating a sinusoidal encoding of the current heading.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: The PI model implemented is that published by Stone et al., 2017.
source: The PI model implemented is that published by Stone et al., 2017.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section with citation.

claim: The core functionality of the PI model arises from the CPU4 neurons that integrate the activation of TN2 neurons that encode the speed of the agent and the inverted activation of direction-sensitive I-TB1 neurons.
source: The core functionality arises from the CPU4 neurons that integrate the activation of TN2 neurons that encode the speed of the agent and the inverted activation of direction-sensitive I-TB1 neurons.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: The result is that the population of CPU4 neurons iteratively track the distance and orientation to the nest (a home vector) in a format akin to a series of directionally locked odometers.
source: The result is that the population of CPU4 neurons iteratively track the distance and orientation to the nest (a home vector) in a format akin to a series of directionally locked odometers.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: The route following model is based on a simple artificial neural network (ANN) with just one hidden layer.
source: The route following model is based on a simple artificial neural network (ANN) with just one hidden layer.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: The input layer of the RF ANN directly takes the amplitudes of the ZM coefficients as the activation in the same way as that of visual projection neurons in MB network.
source: The input layer directly takes the amplitudes of the ZM coefficients as the activation in the same way as that of visual projection neurons in MB network.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Training data for the RF network is derived from the amplitudes and the population encoded phases of the ZM coefficients of the images reconstructed along a habitual route.
source: Training data is derived from the amplitudes and the population encoded phases of the ZM coefficients of the images reconstructed along a habitual route.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: A ring attractor neural network is used to integrate the cues from the VH and PI guidance systems.
source: A ring attractor neural network is used to integrate the cues from the VH and PI guidance systems.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Summation of directional cues represented in vector format leads to optimal angular cue integration which is the same case as real insects.
source: As reported in Hoinville and Wehner, 2018 summation of directional cues represented in vector format leads to optimal angular cue integration which is the same case as real insects.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section with citation.

claim: The number of the integration neurons is set to be 8, constrained by the number of columns in each hemisphere of the insects CX.
source: Constrained by the number of columns in each hemisphere of the insects CX, we set the number of the IN to be 8
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: The visual novelty measured by the MBON provides an ideal signal for context switching with low output when close to the route when RF should dominate versus high output further away from the route when PI and VH should be engaged.
source: The visual novelty measured by the MBON provides an ideal signal for context switching with low output when close to the route when RF should dominate versus high output further away from the route when PI and VH should be engaged (see Figure 2D).
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section with reference to Figure 2D.

claim: The fact that Off-route strategies (PI and VH) compute their turning angles with reference to the global compass whereas the On-route RF strategy is driven with reference to a local compass provides a means to modulate their inputs to the steering circuit independently.
source: Also the fact that Off-route strategies (PI and VH) compute their turning angles with reference to the global compass whereas the On-route RF strategy is driven with reference to a local compass provides a means to modulate their inputs to the steering circuit independently.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Context-dependent switching is realised through a non-linear weighting of the On and Off-route strategies which acts through the same SMP pathway as the VH model.
source: This is realised through a non-linear weighting of the On and Off-route strategies which we propose acts through the same SMP pathway as the VH model (see the SN1 and SN2 neurons in Figure 5A)
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section with reference to Figure 5A.
